newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks open at record high.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks open at record high.

text.p: The Australian share market opened at a record high on Monday after the Dow surged with miner CRA leading the market higher after its sister entity RTZ Plc rose sharply in London trading.

After rising 11.6 points to 2,458.3 shortly after the open, the All Ordinaries index extended its gains to be up 12.8 points at 2,459.5. It had earlier hit an intraday high of 2,459.9, surpassing the previous record of 2,456.7 reached on January 20, 1997.
"It's an impressive start even if volumes are a little low," said a Sydney broker.

"CRA shares are getting a flow-on from RTZ which had some upgrades late last week and the banks are also strong again," he said, noting that Commonwealth Bank continued to lead that sector ahead of its first half results due on Wednesday.

"Commbank has kept on going from Friday. The results from other banks have created some expectations for the CommBank result." CommBank scrip extended Friday's gains to a fresh record high of A$13.75 (US$10.46) in early trade.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about three to one, while about 43 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
